review_text: A small place with good macha and houjicha drinks. They also serve cofee drinks too. The food has a japanese twist to filipino deserts but only if you like matcha.

Really enjoyed the matcha and hojicha. But the matcha turon and matcha grilled cheese were so-so. The place was very beautiful though, with great attention to detail. The laid-back atmosphere is also great for catching up with friends, reading a book, or doing some work.

We got the premium matcha and premium hojicha latte. The taste was really good, very authentic, but for this price, wish the serving was a bit bigger in volume. The place is really nice and cozy. They have a small tatami dining area, alongside the really nicely curated dining area. It has a small japanese country house vibe going on. It has some really nice custom country tables and chairs with cute socks at the feet. Staff was friendly and very accomodating.

Found inside a huge garage. Café was small with indoor and outdoor seating. Just to be safe from the scorching heat of the sun parking was to the side of the wall. Interior was lovely in wood with display of some merchandise for sale. I enjoyed the food as well as the pricey yet tasty matcha. I would definitely drop by when in the area.

Got here via jeep around 3pm. People are occupying the area so sat next to front windows. Had at least two charging spaces. Just ask permission if you are going to remove them. I saw a comment that the Matcha can be expensive and yes, it is. I got a hojicha tea in a teapot ₱165 and hot ceremonial matcha usucha that is Yabukita for ₱195. I can save on the experience this way and I brought some ice cubes to judge whether I will enjoy it hot or cold. I'm just here for the teas anyways. The owners are accommodating with questions especially if you have preferences.

Indahouse cafe captures my heart with the homey ambiance feels…insta-worthy experience in every corner, I so love every details here & the 5-cultivar macha latte which I ordered is really superb! ( not a fan of macha, but this is an exemption…really! ) They also have an ample parking, clean cr, wifi and friendly staffs. It’s a stress free zone and feels like you’re being transported to Japan ….

I don’t usually go to Toril area, but since Indahouse has a pretty strong social media presence and lots of hype online, I decided to drop by while I was in the area. It's a bit hard to spot since the signage is small, but at least parking wasn’t a problem. The place is quite small. It's literally a converted container van but it’s cozy and aesthetic inside. I went on a Sunday and it was packed, which is understandable. There were around 5 to 6 staff that day, so I was surprised it took almost 50 minutes to serve just four drinks (2 matchas and 2 iced coffees). That’s a long wait for just four drinks. Service really needs work. We also asked for the pudding to be packed for takeout, but it was served in a dine-in plate. It took another 10 minutes just to get it repacked. Small thing, but it adds up. The drinks themselves were a letdown. The matcha, priced at ₱250–₱295, came in a small cup that wasn’t even filled to the top. Taste-wise, it wasn’t anything special. The milk overpowered the matcha. There are definitely better and more reasonably priced options elsewhere in Davao. Also worth noting: they don’t give receipts unless you ask, not even a simple POS slip. I really wanted to enjoy my visit, especially because of the great online presence the cafe has. But there’s a noticeable gap between what’s presented on social media and what customers actually experience. If you're going to build a brand with that much visibility, the in-store experience really needs to keep up.
Old town Japanese vibe It must be pretty at night when lights hanged on the tree are lit.

Positives first. Place looks awesome, ambiance is great. We went here because it looked good on instagram. Service is passable. So 0 complains there. Massive negative is the matcha. We are from davao, so there are a lot of matcha places to choose from. Drove all the way to toril because the place looked hype, the matcha looked great. Lasaw ang matcha, taste more like milk than matcha, so the ratio was super off. Worse thing about it is the price. 295 for matcha thats not good at all. Comparing to places like steep or &matcha, where prices are around 250-320, sobrang layo ng quality (although may mas mahal na options sa davao, sobrang layo ng quality compared to here) So if you want to get out davao city and be in a nice place, you can go here. If you want good matcha, this place aint it.

The place is very nice very aesthetic, perfect to stay and talk with friends, or family and perfect for dates, their matcha and hojicha is really good, the matcha pudding is really decadent. the food are also good but more on the expensive side, their curry rice and spaghetti (pinoy style) is delicious and filling. will definitely come back!
Their cafe latte was the best I have tried ever! Staff and owner were very accommodating. Will def be back!

Indahaus is my go-to for good matcha done right. Their okumidori has a deep green colour and tastes smooth all the way through. Big plus that they do oat lattes too — nice to have the option. The place looks good without trying too hard. Well-made furniture and an atmosphere that’s calm but not stiff. Service is friendly and you get what you came for: good drinks, good space, no fuss.

Indahaus feels like a hidden Japanese cabin in the middle of Davao — warm wood, thoughtful, personalised furniture, and an ambience that lets you escape the city without actually leaving it. Their matcha stands out for its clean, pure flavour, and I love that they offer different powders so you can choose exactly how you want it, whether you’re in the mood for something single origin or multiblend cultivars. They also have coffee and hojicha if you feel like mixing it up. Don’t miss the turon, it’s my favourite thing on the menu and the perfect local twist to go with your drink. Service is warm and genuine, thanks to the friendly owners who make you feel like you’re visiting an old friend’s cabin rather than just another café.

Place: Very Instagrammable Staff: friendly and very attentive Matcha: you can explore various types of high quality matcha drink. The flavors make me feel like I’m back in Japan. Special mention to the matcha pudding- oh so heavenly!!

Strongly recommend to try the 5 cultivar matcha, 3 cultivar hojicha with cheesecake and pair it with matcha pudding and the toast with matcha drizzle 👌 Also try the hojicha tea with strawberry (very innovative and shockingly refreshing) Plus the place and vibe is perfect!

I found it a bit underwhelming and overhyped. We only stopped by since it was along the way from an out of town trip. The food and service were fine, but the menu felt overpriced given the location and overall café environment. Nothing really stood out enough to make me want to travel all the way to Toril just for this in the future. The pour over tasted like Kopiko 🫢 That said, it wasn’t a bad experience—just not memorable.
Obsessed with this spot. The Oreo Latte is 10/10, and the view is just as good as the coffee. Super chill atmosphere."
Hidden gem in toril! Beautiful little cafe, in a quiet little spot on the main road! The staff are all awesome too! 😊 …
the AMBIANCE you must SEE and FEEL for yourself... it's TRULY worth your TIME and MONEY... #indahouse

Inda House Café is hands down one of the best places for matcha lovers! 🍵 Their matcha is rich, smooth, and perfectly balanced—not too sweet, so you can really enjoy the authentic flavor. The café itself has a cozy and relaxing vibe, making it a great spot to unwind or catch up with friends. The staff are friendly, and everything feels thoughtfully prepared. If you're looking for one of the best matcha cafés, Inda House Café is definitely worth visiting. Highly recommended!

I won't get bored every day, everything is delicious, the place is beautiful, and the owner's daughter is also very hands-on with her work..keep it up!! It's my birthday tomorrow, I'll be there for my birthday.
The place is beautiful...the food and drinks are delicious, legit, directly from Japan, and the owner's daughter, I think her name is Naomi, is so cute.
